Yes. Not an expensive one.

I'm a sound tech on the weekends, so I care about how things sound. But, I also know enough to understand that there is a VERY quick diminishing return buy buying expensive equipment. (Eg: a 5.1 system is fine. 99+% of people won't be able to hear the difference between a 5.1 system and a 7.2 system. )

Also: you need to get what works best for you. If you spend 95% of your time with video games, then it isn't worth it. Get a 2.1 system.

If you like action movies, then a 5.1 system can be very nice. You can get a Yamaha or Onkyo 5.1 setup for under $400 and it will sound good. Biggest effort will be to run the wiring and make it look nice.

If you are on a tight budget and $400 is too much, then just focus on a 2.1 system. Getting a sub allows for you to hear the frequencies that you otherwise miss. (And, frankly these frequencies can't be produced from a soundbar.)
